title: Redwood + Skyway marketplace integration tech sync
summary: Partner tech sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture artifacts, and joint solution validation. Discussed packaging options (container vs AMI), terraform modules, SSO/KMS integrations, billing models, and a proposed validation plan for private deployments and marketplace procurement flows.
topics: Go-to-market: listing type and joint PR
next_steps: Redwood: share marketplace listing template and sample manifests by 2026-10-23
Skyway: provide test AWS account details and marketplace contact by 2026-10-27
Schedule validation run and perf benchmark week of 2026-11-02
Agree on joint PR draft by 2026-11-09
action_items: Maya Patel - Send Redwood marketplace listing checklist and image requirements - Due: 2026-10-23
Jonah Reed - Prepare reference architecture draft (diagram + terraform example) - Due: 2026-10-30
Evan Cho - Share Skyway test account and marketplace onboarding contact - Due: 2026-10-27
Diego Ramos - Run initial compatibility smoke tests with Redwood container image and share logs - Due: 2026-10-29
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute. um quick roll call?
00:00:07 - Evan Cho: Evan here, hi.
00:00:09 - Lina Morales: Lina on marketplace ops.
00:00:11 - Diego Ramos: Diego, cloud eng.
00:00:13 - Jonah Reed: Jonah, SE from Redwood.
00:00:15 - Priya Kapoor: Priya, platform PM at Redwood.

00:00:20 - Maya Patel: Great. The purpose today is to align on the Skyway marketplace listing and the joint reference arch, plus the validation steps for private deployments. We want to make sure the artifacts we hand to Skyway meet your marketplace team's checklist, and also that our terraform examples reflect how customers will deploy Redwood into a VPC.
00:00:42 - Evan Cho: Sounds good. Lina and I have a few requirements from the marketplace team — image signing, minimum documentation, thumbnail assets, and a licensing flow for SaaS vs BYOL.
00:00:54 - Lina Morales: Also the listing type matters — if it's a SaaS listing we need the redirect endpoints and billing hooks. For AMI/bring-your-own we need AMI IDs and supported regions.
00:01:06 - Jonah Reed: Quick note: Redwood has three deployment models: hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace we can support a container-based image for Skyway's marketplace, and we can also provide AMIs for AWS if you prefer. There was a small hiccup last week with a partner where the AMI metadata didn't include the expected KMS key alias, so we want to avoid that.
00:01:29 - Diego Ramos: That's good to know. On our side we prefer container manifests + terraform modules because it fits into our orchestration. But some enterprise customers will ask for AMI/BYOL images for air-gapped installs.
00:01:42 - Priya Kapoor: We'll include both artifacts. Jonah, can you outline the reference architecture pieces we plan to hand over?
00:01:49 - Jonah Reed: Sure. Draft will include: a reference diagram (control plane vs data plane), terraform example for VPC / subnets / route tables, IAM roles and least-privilege policies, KMS integration notes for KV cache encryption, and instructions for SAML SSO integration and RBAC mapping. Also a performance note: sequence length assumptions and recommended instance types for low-latency inference.
00:02:12 - Lina Morales: On SSO — our marketplace requires SAML metadata and a test SSO provider for validation. Can you provide a test SAML endpoint or a walkthrough?
00:02:20 - Maya Patel: We can provide SAML metadata and a small walk-through doc. For private deployments customers tend to use customer-managed IdPs; we have SAML and OIDC flows documented. We'll include example metadata and a sample SSO provider config.
00:02:33 - Evan Cho: Regarding KMS, do you require a customer-owned KMS key, or do you support using Skyway-managed keys for marketplace customers?
00:02:40 - Jonah Reed: We support both. For Private we recommend customer-managed KMS for compliance. For marketplace SaaS flows, Redwood can manage encryption keys but we can also integrate Skyway KMS via granted policies. We'll note the required key policy in the terraform example.
00:02:55 - Diego Ramos: Also curious about auditing — we need audit logs for inference requests for compliance. Does Redwood provide request-level logging or aggregated metrics only?
00:03:03 - Priya Kapoor: We provide both. Request-level logging can be routed to customer S3 or to your logging endpoint; there are retention controls. For marketplace customers we typically provide a default retention and then the customer can opt-in to longer retention. We'll include details about log formats and sample CloudWatch/S3 manifests.
00:03:22 - Evan Cho: Excellent. On the billing side, what are your recommended marketplace flows? Metered usage, flat subscription, reserved capacity?
00:03:30 - Maya Patel: We offer flexible models. For marketplace we see two common approaches: link to a SaaS subscription with metered billing (calls/tokens), or a marketplace listing for BYOL with reserved capacity contracts handled off-marketplace. We'll work with Lina to understand what Skyway prefers.
00:03:45 - Lina Morales: Skyway prefers a SaaS listing for ease, but enterprise customers will request a reserved option. We'll need to capture both in the listing copy.
00:03:54 - Jonah Reed: On the technical validation, our proposed plan: provide container image in ECR and a terraform module. Skyway runs a smoke deploy into a test account, we'll run a small benchmark (throughput and 95th percentile latency) using Redwood's perf harness. Then iterate on instance types and batching configs.
00:04:12 - Diego Ramos: That works. What perf harness are you using? Is it open source?
00:04:16 - Jonah Reed: It's our internal harness but we have a simplified open repo with the benchmark scripts we'll share. It simulates typical chat loads and also runs tokenized load tests. Note: the harness assumes KV caching will be enabled for streaming workloads; if your customer disables cache for privacy reasons, latencies will be higher.
00:04:34 - Evan Cho: Privacy — one of our regulated customers requires no external egress, so they'd do an air-gapped install. Do you support on-prem packaging?
00:04:42 - Priya Kapoor: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem air-gapped installs. For those cases we provide a tarball/container bundle plus a signed manifest and offline license activation. We'll need details about the customer's network and storage for the runbook.
00:04:55 - Lina Morales: For listing assets, we need high-resolution logos, product screenshots, and a 200-300 word summary. Also we need a short video or gif.
00:05:04 - Maya Patel: We'll prepare assets. Jonah, can you capture a couple of screenshots from the console and a short demo gif?
00:05:10 - Jonah Reed: Yep, I'll capture those. Quick caveat: some of the UI labels in the console might be slightly different in the private build; transcription sometimes shows Redwood Dedicate instead of Dedicated, so I'll ensure copy is accurate.
00:05:22 - Evan Cho: Small question — region coverage. Does Redwood have supported regions list? We need to know which AWS regions your images are pre-pulled in.
00:05:30 - Jonah Reed: We'll include a supported-regions matrix. For AMIs we'll give region AMI IDs; for ECR images we can provide multi-arch tags.
00:05:38 - Diego Ramos: For terraform modules, do you publish a public registry module or do you expect vendors to copy into their infra repo?
00:05:44 - Priya Kapoor: We'll publish an example module in our GitHub and provide a versioned terraform module. Most customers vendor the module into their infra repo but the registry module makes it easier.
00:05:55 - Lina Morales: On certification — Skyway requires a simple checklist completion signed by an engineer before listing. Can you commit to how long validation will take?
00:06:04 - Maya Patel: If we get the artifacts by 10/23, we can schedule validation the week of 11/02 and complete it in 1-2 weeks depending on any remediation. So target go-live mid-November.
00:06:15 - Evan Cho: That timeline works for us.
00:06:18 - Jonah Reed: Quick technical detail: network egress. For Private deployments we allow inbound-only control plane? There was a partner who needed strict egress controls — we have a mode that routes control plane traffic to a customer-managed proxy. We'll document how to configure the proxy and the minimal endpoints that must be reachable for license verification.
00:06:37 - Diego Ramos: Good — we'll need that in the runbook.
00:06:40 - Priya Kapoor: Another point: telemetry and quality monitoring — Redwood Optimize can push model quality alerts if you give us evaluation prompt sets. For joint customers we can provide a sample eval suite.
00:06:51 - Evan Cho: Are there any known incompatibilities with Skyway's default networking setups?
00:06:56 - Jonah Reed: The main friction is strict MTU or restrictive egress firewalls; also customers using very old kernel versions on AMIs have occasional GLIBC mismatch with our runtime. We'll add an explicit minimum OS/kernel note.
00:07:10 - Lina Morales: For the listing copy — can we have a technical bullet list that highlights latency SLOs, supported instance types, and security certifications like SOC 2?
00:07:19 - Maya Patel: Yes. Redwood is SOC 2 compliant and we can provide the certification and audit logs guidance. We'll include latency SLOs as guidance, not guaranteed in the marketplace copy unless we have a dedicated SLA.
00:07:32 - Evan Cho: Competitor note — some customers compare to HashiCorp's managed runtimes; how should we position differentiation?
00:07:39 - Maya Patel: Focus on unified inference across hosted/dedicated/private and the cost/performance tooling. We'll give Lina a short positioning paragraph.
00:07:48 - Diego Ramos: Ok next, on technical deliverables can you enumerate exact files you will send?
00:07:53 - Jonah Reed: We'll send: 1) listing assets (logo, screenshots, gif), 2) AMI manifest + ECR image tags, 3) terraform example + module link, 4) reference architecture diagram (PNG + draw.io), 5) SAML metadata and SSO walkthrough, 6) perf harness scripts and sample results, 7) runbook for air-gapped installs, 8) SOC 2 cert and security whitepaper.
00:08:19 - Evan Cho: Great. I'll make sure Skyway's marketplace contact is cc'd on the incoming ticket.
00:08:24 - Lina Morales: One small ask — can Redwood provide a short customer-facing FAQ for the listing to reduce support noise?
00:08:30 - Priya Kapoor: Yes, we'll produce an FAQ doc with common questions about billing, security, deployment models.
00:08:36 - Maya Patel: Alright let's capture next steps — Maya to send checklist, Jonah to draft ref arch, Evan to share test account, Diego to run smoke tests. Anything else?
00:08:47 - Evan Cho: Nothing from me.
00:08:49 - Lina Morales: Looks good.
00:08:51 - Diego Ramos: I'll start the smoke tests once we get the image.
00:08:55 - Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the validation week and upload the initial artifacts to the shared folder.
00:09:02 - Jonah Reed: Thanks all.
00:09:05 - [meeting ends]
